fl-pinellas-2026-school-board-d3-campogn.name: Curtis Campogni
fl-pinellas-2026-school-board-d3-campogn.bio: Founder of Speak4MC, a communication-training firm; former case manager and youth transition program leader.

positions.stance: Says schools will likely close but the Board should set clear, public guardrails for weighing closure factors before choosing individual schools.
Proposes a "Student Impact Test" so spending farthest from direct student outcomes gets the most scrutiny before cuts.
"The Superintendent manages the district. The Board governs it"; Board should set priorities, guardrails and hold the Superintendent accountable.
"Hear them. Empower them. Pay them."; supports clearer criteria and transparency for teacher contract renewal decisions.
Open to exploring weapon-detection technology where it can be implemented effectively, learning from problems in previous pilots.

fl-pinellas-2026-school-board-d3-peters-.name: Dawn Peters
fl-pinellas-2026-school-board-d3-peters-.bio: Pinellas County School Board member since 2022 and Vice Chairperson; previously worked in property management.

positions.stance: Believes "public education is fundamental to our constitutional republic" and should instill civic responsibility and critical thinking.
Committed to "transparency, accountability, and responsible governance," ensuring families have a voice and tax dollars are used wisely.
Supports pathways after graduation, including college readiness, career and technical education, skilled trades, military service, or direct workforce entry.
Works with local, state and federal leaders, PTAs and community stakeholders to strengthen schools and support educators.

fl-pinellas-2026-st-petersburg-mayor-cri.name: Charlie Crist
fl-pinellas-2026-st-petersburg-mayor-cri.bio: Former Florida legislator, Education Commissioner, Attorney General, Governor and U.S. Representative.

positions.stance: "Improving communication to ensure every resident can tap into their local government's resources."
"Affordability is the number one issue facing our City."
"There is a better way to respond and recover."
"The Mayor must lead the charge on economic development."
"The pathway to long-term success is through education."
Focuses on increasing housing supply, protecting existing residents, and expanding down payment assistance and homeowner stability programs.
Supports "a balanced approach to public safety that prioritizes accountability, innovation, and trust."
Supports expanding workforce training partnerships, such as with St. Petersburg College, connecting residents to jobs and careers.
Advancing stormwater, drainage, flood mitigation and hardened infrastructure investments to prepare the city for future storms.
Supports small business grants, technical assistance and funding for minority- and women-owned businesses so prosperity is shared.
Supports stronger storm communication, accessible resources for vulnerable residents, climate-ready infrastructure and neighborhood-level resilience planning.
Supports fair access to city services and removing barriers that disproportionately affect marginalized communities.
Supports housing stability for families and seniors, protections for renters, and pathways to homeownership.
"Growth is inevitable, displacement is absolutely not"; supports development respecting neighborhood character and transparent planning.
Commits to clear communication, accessible public meetings and materials, and systems that make participation easier.

fl-pinellas-2026-st-petersburg-council-d.name: Gabriel Hament
fl-pinellas-2026-st-petersburg-council-d.bio: Assistant Public Defender; former investment advisor representative for nonprofit organizations.

positions.stance: Supports the proposed $600 million bond for stormwater and wastewater improvements and a grant program for residential storm hardening.
Supports matching grants for storm hardening and requiring affordable units when development concessions are granted.
Will focus on enhancing public spaces, expanding parks, and securing funds for a District 2 community center.
Will keep St. Pete's "intangible local culture" in mind in new development planning and decision-making.

fl-pinellas-2026-st-petersburg-council-d.name: Linsey Grove
fl-pinellas-2026-st-petersburg-council-d.bio: Public health advocate, educator and small business owner; former president of the League of Women Voters of the St. Petersburg Area.

positions.stance: Supports more affordable housing options, repair programs to reduce displacement, and limiting private equity purchases of single-family homes.
Supports updating stormwater infrastructure, expanded transit and bike lanes, and zoning allowing affordable housing and density near transit.
Supports more help for neighborhood associations and easier resident access to city resources and meetings.

fl-pinellas-2026-st-petersburg-council-d.name: Trevor Mallory
fl-pinellas-2026-st-petersburg-council-d.bio: Former professional baseball player and President of Neighborhood Home Solutions; served on the city's Affordable Housing Advisory Committee.

positions.stance: Works with government and nonprofits so people can access affordable financing to buy a home and build wealth.
Opposes "experimental AI data centers" in St. Petersburg, citing higher electric bills, water use and noise.
Supports infrastructure investment against disasters, faster permitting for rebuilding, and protecting green spaces and tree canopy.
Will work to expand the city's youth recreation programs and opportunities beyond athletics.
Will ensure first responders have needed tools and resources, and that more come from the communities they serve.
